what: Fortinet sells network security. Its FortiGate firewalls sit at the edge of corporate networks and branch offices, and it layers cloud security, secure access and security operations software on top.
customers: Enterprises, governments and service providers in more than 100 countries, often mid-sized organisations buying a full security package from one vendor.
money: FortiGate firewall appliances built on its own custom chips
security subscriptions and support attached to installed appliances
moat: Custom silicon that lets its firewalls run security functions cheaper and faster than software-only rivals, plus an installed base that renews subscriptions for years.
risks: Firewall hardware sales are lumpy and were hit by a long inventory digestion period
Security spending is shifting toward cloud-native vendors
Competition in secure access and cloud security is intense
Growth has settled into the mid teens from much faster earlier rates
opportunities: Return on invested capital above 70% shows unusually efficient economics
Service subscriptions renew on an installed base of millions of devices
Secure access service edge is a new growth area where it can sell to existing customers
watch: Billings rather than revenue, since subscriptions are recognised over time, and unified access growth.
